cards.title: ⚠️⚠️ Order lookup by client id returned SOMEONE ELSE'S order — Alpaca ignores `client_order_ids`
cards.notes:
SHIPPED 2026-08-02. MEASURED against the live paper API while probing for an unrelated thread: `GET /v2/orders?client_order_ids=X` IGNORES the param entirely — a total-garbage value returned the SAME four open orders as no filter at all — and the list defaults to status=open, so any closed order is invisible. `aget_order_by_client_id` therefore answered "did MY order reach the broker?" with whatever open order happened to be first, typically a resting protective stop on another symbol.

THREE callers read that as evidence about ONE specific order:
- reconcile_pending_executions: binds our execution row to a STRANGER's broker_order_id, after which reconcile tracks someone else's order to decide our fill (wrong symbol/qty/side/attribution).
- aplace_order 409 recovery: returns a stranger's order as the placement. _parse_post_response maps EVERY 422 to conflict (wash trade, insufficient qty — not just duplicate ids), so an order that was never placed could be reported `submitted` against another order's id.
- _exit_may_be_live (worst): decides whether a released protective stop goes back on. With any other resting order in the account it concluded "the exit is live" and left the position BARE; with none it concluded the opposite and would stack a stop on a live full-size sell.

FIX: the singular `GET /v2/orders:by_client_order_id`, None only on a 404 that NAMES the id (a route-level 404 carries the same status AND numeric code — measured — and now propagates). Verified live id-for-id on six real rows; closed orders resolve; a never-placed id returns clean None. No damage in the ledger (zero duplicate broker ids, zero submitted rows missing one).

SAME FAMILY, same probe: get_open_orders sent no `limit`, so it was silently capped at Alpaca's default 50 (`limit` IS honoured — measured). That list is where pending_sell comes from, so past 50 open orders in one account a resting sell vanishes and reads as free shares. Now asks the 500 max and logs loudly on truncation.

ALSO enabled by this: _exit_may_be_live tested EXISTENCE, not liveness. Now that closed orders resolve, a place POST that timed out on the wire but was REJECTED at the broker came back as a real order and left the position bare — it now restores stops for canceled/rejected/expired and treats anything unrecognised as live.

Memory: alpaca-order-list-lies.

cards.title: Nothing outside paper ever ENDED a stuck execution row — the reconciler does now, on corroborated absence
cards.notes:
SHIPPED 2026-08-02 (HANDOFF thread, opened by the sell-reservation round). Three ways a row could never reach a terminal status: the pending sweep filtered execution_mode='paper' (submit writes `pending` BEFORE it branches on mode, so a crash strands a row of ANY mode); reconcile_open_executions logged and `continue`d forever when a row had no broker_order_id; and again whenever the broker read raised. A row that can never end keeps consuming risk budget and keeps reserving shares against later sells.

WHAT SHIPPED: sweep covers every mode; a row with no broker id is RECOVERED via our own client id (and gets submitted_at, without which it escapes both reservation bounds); dry_run short-circuits with no broker call; 404 is typed as evidence while every other read failure keeps polling.

★ REVIEW A REFRAMED IT. 'rejected' is the codebase's word for "never reached the broker", and a WRONG terminalisation unwinds four gates at once: list_open_protective_stops drops the row so a live stop can no longer be RELEASED (position un-exitable while the stop guard pages it bare); count_executions_today / sum_today_notional / sum_inflight_notional all drop it, freeing budget a live order still uses; the auto-entry dedup re-opens on a symbol that already has a live order; and proposals marks the proposal failed. The answer was STRONGER EVIDENCE, not a bigger blast radius: absence must be CORROBORATED by two independent routes (the order-id route AND the client-id route must both say absent). That also self-heals a wrong broker_order_id by repointing the row — exactly the damage the old client-id lookup could write (see broker-order-lookup-by-client-id).

Also from review: the risk-check audit trail is MERGED not overwritten (it is the only record of which gates let a real-money order through); an account-less sweep can no longer reject a foreign row; a poison-pill timestamp can no longer raise out of the row loop and kill the whole account's poll (which would silently disable protective-stop placement every cycle).

The two sum_inflight_sell_qty heuristics were NOT retired. They fail toward not-reserving, so they cannot lock a position, and they are what still holds if the reconcile itself is down — backstops now rather than the mechanism. Retiring them needs its own measured round.

15 guards kill-switched RED (five were green on the first pass — four masked by the corroboration path itself). On current live state both mechanisms act on ZERO rows. Follow-ups in HANDOFF: a distinct `orphaned` terminal that still counts toward the caps; get_broker_for_account's silent fallback to default credentials.

cards.title: Native chart candle fidelity: pixel-grid geometry (wick lean / body-width flicker) + the live-rollover phantom gap
cards.notes: SHIPPED + DEPLOYED :3001 2026-07-29 (BUILD_ID 17:09). Detail in the BUILD_LOG 2026-07-29 row. TWO unrelated bugs behind one founder report. (1) GEOMETRY: candle body (fillRect, per-edge Math.round) and wick (line, floor(x*dpr)+0.5) snapped to DIFFERENT pixel grids -> wick sat +/-0.5 device px off centre and flipped sides bar-to-bar at 81/169 spacings at dpr 1 (21/169 at dpr 2 -- halved, NOT gone); candleBodyWidth rounded only the first term of min(round(sp*0.7), sp-2) so widths went fractional below ~6.7px spacing -> alternating 3px/4px bodies in ONE frame (70/341 zooms); wick tips left fractional in Y. Fix = one Painter.barColumn(x, barSpacing) in the adapter: single snapped centre shared by body/wick/volume/MACD-hist, body width forced to the wick's PARITY (an even body has no middle column, so the wick must pick a side -- that flip WAS the artifact). Measured: lean 0.5 -> 0, multi-width frames 70/341 -> 0, no touching bodies, default view byte-identical (5px body). Canvas CSS box now pinned to bitmap/dpr + engine rounds its logical size (resampling path closed -- FLAGGED BUT NEVER CONFIRMED LIVE, fixed because it is 3 lines). (2) THE GAP THE FOUNDER ACTUALLY MEANT: refetch every 30s vs client bars-cache TTL 60s (1Min) / 180s (5Min), so most refreshes were cache HITS -- the same payload re-mapped and setBars replacing the array wholesale, wiping live ticks and DELETING the forming candle when the snapshot predated the bucket; the next tick (~100ms, quotes at 10 Hz) rolled over again and re-opened it at the CURRENT price => gap = all movement since the snapshot (<=30s on 1m, <=3min on 5m). Same family as chart-stale-merge-fix (07-06) but a distinct mechanism (that was the >=2-interval staleness gate; this is a cache hit regressing the tail INSIDE the freshness window). Fix = skip re-applying an already-applied payload object + new pure mergeFetchedBars(fetched, local) in chart-engine/merge.ts (vendor wins; local bars survive only strictly past the payload's last bar, so no dupes/reorder). 22 new tests (17 geometry invariants across dpr 1/1.5/2, 5 merge-contract); 80 engine tests, tsc + eslint clean on touched files. FOUNDER VERIFY: watch a 1m/5m chart through several bucket switches -- gap should be gone. Follow-ups, NOT done (notes only, no new cards): inter-candle gaps still alternate 1 device px (inherent to fractional bar spacing, TV same); at dpr 1 spacing 3.05-3.95 renders bare wicks (no odd body fits without merging); autoscale recomputes the price range every frame, so a fast tape can still shimmer sub-pixel (design question, not a bug); futures 1H buckets on UTC hours so a session's first hourly bar spans 30min (equities use Alpaca native 1H, unaffected); Recharts surfaces (equity-chart / pnl-chart / /charts) were never reviewed this round.

cards.title: Options sampler breadth tier — wide IV-only lane so the cross-section is hundreds of names, not 37
cards.notes: Study B (IV_LEVEL_PREREG_2026-07-25.md) measured the blocker precisely: the IV-level effect is real and robust across 2,112 names (+0.0418 even under a 60% IV ceiling) and ABSENT on our own 37 (-0.0004). Not the phenomenon -- the size of the cross-section. So the sampler gained a two-tier universe. deep = the whole banded board + open interest, for names we might actually trade (unchanged behaviour). wide = an IV reading ONLY: a filtered chain slice (expiry window bracketing 30 DTE + strike band at the same +/-25% moneyness), no per-contract rows, no OI call. Measured: ~0.06s and ONE row per wide symbol vs ~0.3-0.9s and ~1,100 rows deep -- breadth is essentially free, depth is what costs. Verified three ways before registering anything: (1) the wide SLICE reproduces the deep BOARD's 30d constant-maturity IV EXACTLY (0.000% deviation across 12 names) because the strike band already contains every strike the ATM interpolation reaches; (2) our iv30 agrees with the independent DoltHub corpus on the same session within 2.2% median across 15 names -- and note the offset is CONSISTENTLY POSITIVE (~+2% on all 15), a systematic method difference, so the two sources must never be naively pooled in a level study; (3) a full 627-symbol sweep ran in 63s, 566/574 wide rows carrying a usable iv30 (the 8 misses REFUSED rather than fabricated, per the no-extrapolation rule). Append-only safety: wide registration NEVER demotes a deep symbol (breadth must not cost depth on a name we hold), deep registration promotes a wide one, and both are regression-tested. iv_daily gained a tier column because a wide row's volume/OI zeros are PLACEHOLDERS, not measurements -- a reader must check tier before aggregating anything but IV/HV/VRP. Universe resolver (tools/resolve_wide_universe.py) sources the DoltHub corpus symbol list deliberately: those names already carry up to 7 years of history, so a level baseline exists on day one instead of 2027, and a symbol is registered only if Alpaca actually returns contracts (append-only means a delisted ticker admitted here would sit in the sweep forever). ⚠️ Vendor pages the chain ALPHABETICALLY even with range filters -- SPY on one page came back 7/10/11-DTE only and could not bracket 30 DTE; wide fetches allow 5 pages. This is perception infrastructure, not a strategy gate: it serves IV-level as a labeled angle in the fusion layer regardless of whether options-income-lane ever opens.

cards.title: Kronos probe — ANSWERED: no. Both legs failed, package deleted per pre-registration
cards.notes: Kronos (github.com/shiyu-coder/Kronos, AAAI'26, MIT) = pretrained autoregressive model over OHLCV candles; sampling it many times yields a CONDITIONAL distribution of future paths. Read on the paper: headline '93% RankIC' is 0.0254 vs 0.0138 (factor-scale, Chinese A-shares/SSE 15-min); on return forecasting it beats the best baseline by only 17% (0.0622 vs 0.0533); its best task is volatility, where the runner-up is GARCH at 9% MAE. Every use case has a cheap classical baseline right behind it — so the ONLY question worth asking is whether its conditional path shape beats an unconditional vol-matched block bootstrap. Value if it passes: a cold-start prior for P(target before stop) on a NEW idea type, before the ledger has graded anything (calibration-counts-everything gives us win% only after a track record exists). Probe is PRE-REGISTERED in research/kronos_probe/README.md: 10 symbols, 5-min RTH bars, 512-bar context, H=12 bars, symmetric ±1σ barriers, 3-way outcome, 200 paths/arm, multiclass log-loss with a paired block-bootstrap CI over session dates. PASS iff Kronos's log-loss is lower AND the 95% CI excludes 0 — anything else deletes the package. LEAKAGE is the live hazard (12B candles from 45 exchanges; no stated cutoff; paper tests 2024-07..2025-06): primary window is post-cutoff 2025-09..2026-07, and the SAME harness runs a pre-cutoff 2023 window so the gap between them estimates memorization instead of fearing it. ISOLATION: separate .venv-kronos (torch NEVER in requirements.txt), upstream cloned not vendored, probe reads SQLite directly so it imports zero product code; removal is rm -rf of one directory. Calibration found + fixed 3 real issues BEFORE any scoring: upstream predict() averages its samples and collapses the distribution being measured (we call generate() with the context on the BATCH dim instead); top_p=0.9 truncation made paths 0.61x too narrow (now 1.0 → 0.97x); and our own sigma estimate swept in 7 overnight gaps per 512-bar context, inflating it up to 2.46x worst on high-vol days (barriers.intraday_log_returns). Related but distinct: per-symbol-volatility (EWMA estimator for SIZING) — Kronos is not a candidate there unless this probe passes. NOTE 07-24: the probe's vol leg runs at 5-min/1-hour, which does NOT settle the per-symbol-volatility card's DAILY deferral — vol results don't transfer across frequencies (intraday is dominated by the U-shape neither estimator models). The daily bake-off is its own cheap CPU-only module, research/vol_bakeoff.py (no GPU, no Kronos). SECOND LEG added 07-24 (founder catch: the probe as built would spend a full GPU day without answering the vol question): Kronos's implied sigma is a FREE byproduct of the same rollouts, so the run now also scores it against EWMA and GARCH(1,1) on QLIKE — separate pre-registered rule requiring it to beat BOTH (beating only the weaker baseline is a FAIL), reported independently so neither test launders the other's null; a path-FAIL + vol-WIN demotes to a bake-off input on per-symbol-volatility, not a pass. GARCH refit per point, fail-soft, +8 min on a ~23h run. NEXT: run primary + leakage windows, then PASS/FAIL per the two pre-registered rules. NIGHTLY PASS 07-25 (1h bars, next-session horizon; own pre-registration in NIGHTLY_README.md, committed before scoring): BOTH LEGS FAIL. Path test: Kronos log-loss 1.2483 vs bootstrap 1.0922, delta +0.1561 CI [+0.1150,+0.1973] — CI excludes 0 on the WRONG side, i.e. ~14% WORSE than an unconditional bootstrap. It is a SHAPE failure, not a scale artifact: mean P(timeout) 0.6476 vs 0.6480 (actual 0.5137), so the arms agreed on how often barriers get touched and disagreed on when/which way. Vol leg FAIL: QLIKE Kronos -5.914 vs EWMA -6.618 vs GARCH -6.752 — BUT that is a LEVEL error, not an information failure: one global rescale per arm makes Kronos vs EWMA a dead tie (-0.0025, CI [-0.1011,+0.0824]). Cause is partly ours — calibrate.py samples ONE symbol; T=0.7 read 1.00x on AAPL but the universe median is 0.741 (GOOGL 0.921 .. META 0.604), so calibrate across symbols if this harness is reused. Deliberately NOT re-run: recalibrating after seeing a FAIL is the laundering pre-registration exists to prevent. Leakage window NOT run (pre-registered as conditional on a path PASS). Two parameters INVERTED vs the 5-min probe, both measured before scoring: gaps are SIGNAL at this horizon (H=7 crosses exactly one) so sigma/bootstrap/outcome all go gap-inclusive; and T=1.0 samples 1.38x too WIDE here (5-min was 0.61x too narrow) so T=0.7. Cost measured: 1.08 s/eval point on the 4090 (36.7 min for 2,040 points) — a production nightly would be ~4 GPU-minutes, so cost was never the blocker, decision quality was. BONUS independent of Kronos: GARCH beats EWMA at 1h/next-session (ewma-garch +0.1338, CI [+0.0339,+0.2405]) — does NOT settle per-symbol-volatility, which defers on DAILY bars. NEXT: nothing further chartered for Kronos by this work; the 5-min primary/leakage run on serv is the remaining open question. || CLOSED 2026-07-25 — BOTH configurations FAILED BOTH LEGS, package deleted per the README's own removal rule. cards.title: Per-symbol volatility model → regime perception + vol-targeted sizing (v1, EWMA)
cards.notes: GAP found 2026-07-24 (traced from a GARCH question): the app has ZERO per-symbol volatility — regime perception is one market-wide VIX/curve read (signals/regime.py, FRED, rule-based), and there is NO volatility in the sizing math (mechanical sizing = pure notional_pct/notional_usd via signals/strategy_scan.py:99 _resolve_notional; notional→shares = floor(notional/price) at trading/proposal_intake.py:_size_candidate ~:120). RiskEngine only GATES qty, never sizes it. LLM books self-size (research/book_driver.py notional) and are book_uncapped in RiskEngine (:501); interactive chat hands over raw qty. So the two places vol matters most — per-symbol regime + the sizing seam — are both empty. BUILD SPEC (brief tools/composer-bridge/briefs/per-symbol-volatility.md): v1 estimator = EWMA (RiskMetrics λ=0.94), NOT GARCH — deliberate (clustering is the value; zero deps; deterministic; fail-soft; keyless/multi-user). GARCH(1,1) DEFERRAL NOW SETTLED 2026-07-24 — KEEP EWMA. Ran the daily bake-off (research/vol_bakeoff.py, CPU-only, no GPU/Kronos): 85 symbols, 169,185 symbol-days over ~10.5y of Alpaca daily bars, walk-forward one-day-ahead, QLIKE, paired CI resampled over DATES. GARCH beat EWMA by a mean of just 0.0107 QLIKE with 95% CI [-0.0348, +0.0129] — STRADDLES ZERO, so the pre-registered tie rule (EWMA wins ties as the zero-dependency incumbent) keeps EWMA. GARCH does NOT earn the arch dependency for daily sizing; do not re-open without a NEW pre-registered question (e.g. a specific regime slice, pre-registered, not post-hoc). ⚠ the first run returned EWMA QLIKE 4.4e10 — a BUG, not a result: NBIS/Nebius was halted ~2.5y (636 zero returns/2610 bars), decaying EWMA variance to 1e-9 so one symbol swamped 170k points; fixed with a halt guard + sigma floor applied to BOTH arms. Parts: (1) signals/volatility.py — forecast_vol(symbol, bars)→VolForecast{daily_sigma, annualized, regime calm|normal|storm via self-relative 33/80 pctile, as_of}; fail-soft None below MIN_OBS=40; LOOKAHEAD GUARD = completed daily bars only (drop today's partial bar, daily-bar-baseline-trap), reuse the bar-dated-today pattern from risk_engine._rest_quote_price. (2) trading/proposal_intake.py:_size_candidate — mult=clamp(target_annual_vol/forecast.annualized, 0.25, 1.5) applied to config notional BEFORE floor; MECHANICAL ONLY + opt-in per-strategy vol_target flag (default off, strategy-off-by-default); books+chat EXCLUDED (self-size + book_uncapped amplification risk); fail-soft=identity 1.0; Decimal at the seam; clamp is the safety (storm shrinks, calm capped, RiskEngine still gates — never past a cap). (3) config volatility{enabled:false,target_annual_vol:0.20,clamp_lo:0.25,clamp_hi:1.5,ewma_lambda:0.94} + log vol_regime/vol_annualized/size_multiplier on the candidate (calibration-counts-everything; log never fabricate). Rollout: shadow (log-only) → paper opt-in on ONE strategy → perception dot (own card). Review before commit = TWO split-mandate Opus. || 07-24 PARKED (founder). cards.title: Chart bars: incremental refresh + broadened prewarm + reload-persistent frontend cache
cards.notes: Draft PR (worktree). Root cause of 'watchlist charts still slow on some timeframes' (chart perf audit): the prewarm loop re-walked the ENTIRE `days` range on every TTL expiry, so keeping a series warm cost as much as a cold load - which is why prewarm scope had to stay pinned to the 1Day default only (storm invariant, see chart-bars-prewarm-storms). Fix: _fetch_bars now dispatches incremental-vs-full. A warm series with a fresh full baseline re-fetches only a small trailing window (_BARS_INCREMENTAL_DAYS, 2-90d by timeframe) and merges it over the cached bars - still-forming last bar overwritten, new bars appended; ascending same-provider ISO times so the concat stays sorted+deduped. Full re-baseline forced hourly (_BARS_FULL_REBASELINE) so split adjustments / history revisions propagate. Empty window / provider error / inc>=days -> fall back to a full walk (which owns the resilience + stale-if-error fallbacks). ENABLER for #2 (prewarm more than the default timeframe) without outrunning the TTLs. tests/test_bars_cache.py +3 (merge, hourly rebaseline, empty->full); 8/8 module + 53 adjacent green; ruff clean. Deploy + founder verify pending. || FIX #2 (same PR): prewarm now broadcasts the K most-recently-used distinct specs (_BARS_HOT_SPECS_MAX=2, ~the timeframes you're actively in) across the WHOLE watchlist, not just the 1Day default — so switching symbols/timeframes is served warm. This is the seen-specs x symbols cross-product the 07-22 storm forbade, affordable now ONLY because fix #1 makes each warm refresh cheap. Bounded two ways: K hot specs + a hard _BARS_PREWARM_MAX_ENTRIES=160 cap trimmed from the tail (1Day baseline never sacrificed; hot slots go to most-recently-viewed symbols, never an alphabetical SPY/TSLA clip). Cap trims are logged (no silent caps). tests: replaced the old 'no cross-product' pin with 3 new (broadcast, K-bound, entry-cap+recency+log); 10/10 module + 53 adjacent green, ruff clean. Tunable: K and MAX_ENTRIES. Still open: #3 persist frontend bars-cache across reloads. || FIX #3 (same PR, frontend): the in-memory bars cache (frontend/lib/bars-cache.ts) is now mirrored to sessionStorage — rehydrate on load, flush on tab-hide (pagehide + visibilitychange->hidden) — so a full page reload (F5, restored tab) no longer drops every chart to cold. Transparent to callers: fetchBarsCached still applies the TTL, so a rehydrated-but-expired entry refetches exactly as before; the win is instant paint on a within-TTL reload. sessionStorage (not local) = survives reload/same-tab-nav, clears on tab close; all access best-effort/guarded (private-mode/quota -> cold start). Tricky logic (byte-budget eviction newest-first, corrupt-blob tolerance) factored into pure dependency-free frontend/lib/bars-cache-persist.ts + 5 vitest tests (glob broadened one line). 57/57 vitest + typecheck clean. ALL THREE audit fixes now in this PR; #3 backstop budget 3.5MB. || 07-23 MERGED (PR #102 -> 0756de3) after orchestrator line-by-line review + TWO split-mandate Opus adversarial passes (both approve-with-nits). Deferred follow-ups (reviewer LOWs): backward clock-step bypasses TTL age checks; dev-HMR listener stacking; double-flush serialize on tab-hide; per-key rebaseline jitter (synchronized hourly cohort); truncated tail guard. Deploy + live verify (bars_prewarm lag_s, WAF quiet) pending gauge window.

cards.title: ⚠️ No holiday calendar — a market holiday in the exit window can hold a position THROUGH its print
cards.notes:
Found 2026-07-16 while verifying the live deploy. trading/market_hours.py is self-described 'v1 — weekdays only, no holiday calendar' with a `# TODO: Alpaca /v2/clock for holidays` on BOTH is_market_open and is_after_close. And research/strategy_features.py::_trading_days_until is HOLIDAY-NAIVE by its own docstring ('Mon-Fri count... May drift ~1-2 days vs the real calendar'). 
★ WHY THIS IS NOW A FAT TAIL, NOT A ROUNDING ERROR: earnings_drift is LIVE + auto, and its entire safety property is 'exit exactly 1 trading day before the print, never hold through it'. A holiday inside the window makes td OVERCOUNT (it counts the holiday as a trading day) — we think we have 2 days when we have 1. Then ON the holiday, is_market_open() wrongly returns True (it's a weekday), the bmo rule fires at 15:45, and the order QUEUES to the next session's open — **which is the print day**. That is holding through the announcement: the exact event exit_lead_td=1 exists to prevent. 
✅ NOT A RISK THIS SEASON: no US equity market holidays between 2026-07-16 and Labor Day (2026-09-07), so the whole Q2 window is clean. ⚠️ It bites in the Q4-earnings window — MLK Day sits in mid-January. Fix before then; don't let a bad fill discover it. 
FIX: Alpaca /v2/clock (or its calendar endpoint) for the real session calendar, wired into BOTH market_hours and _trading_days_until — they must agree or the two gates disagree about what a trading day is. Cache it; it's static per day.

✅ IN PROGRESS 2026-07-16 (branch fix/market-holiday-calendar): built a pure-Python NYSE calendar (trading/market_calendar.py) rather than wiring Alpaca /v2/clock — keyless/offline (no vendor-account gating, matches the EDGAR ethos) and NO network in the hot scan path where _trading_days_until runs. Algorithmic 10 annual holidays w/ observed shifts + Good Friday (Computus) + an _AD_HOC_CLOSURES set for the un-computable ones (Sandy, Bush, Carter). Verified against known NYSE closures 2010-2026 (18 spot-checks + oracle test). Wired into market_hours.py (all 3 fns) and _trading_days_until. Scope = FULL-day closures only; half-day early-CLOSE times are a documented non-goal (only cost: is_market_open reads True for the 13:00-16:00 tail on ~3 days/yr). LEFT OUT (siblings sharing the naive-weekday bug, lower stakes, follow-ups): brokers/market_clock.py session labels, research/idea_tracker.py idea-expiry. 131 tests green, ruff clean. Pending 1 adversarial review + PR.

cards.title: Notional orders — buy $X worth, let the broker do the fractional shares (chokepoint PR)
cards.notes:
Founder 2026-07-16: 'why not just buy 10000 worth and allow fractional shares'. Correct — Alpaca supports NOTIONAL orders natively (send a dollar amount, broker computes fractional shares; market + TIF=day only, which is exactly our case). It's also what the backtest models: research/portfolio.py sizes per_trade_fraction x equity with NO share granularity at all. 
TODAY: trading/proposal_intake.py:81 does `qty = floor(notional_usd / price)` ourselves; brokers/base.py PlaceOrderRequest has `qty` and no `notional`; the adapter body sends qty only. 
GAIN IS SMALL on deployment — measured at $10k/position over the live sp500: avg **98.8%** deployed, worst 65.0% (NVR $6,498 -> 1 share), 0 names unbuyable => ~+0.24pp CAGR. NOT the reason to do it. 
★ THE REAL REASON — the `qty < 1 -> {'status':'too_small'}` drop (proposal_intake.py:90) is EQUITY-DEPENDENT and biases the recovery. notional_pct=10 means the dollar size SHRINKS with equity: at $100k every S&P name is buyable, but at $60k NVR ($6,498) becomes unbuyable and silently leaves the universe; lower still and AZO/FIX/GWW/SNDK follow. **The strategy's universe quietly narrows exactly when it's performing worst.** Notional removes the failure mode at any account size. 
It also SIMPLIFIES the chokepoint: max_order_value_usd is checked as qty x price today; with notional you compare the dollar figure directly, and the integral-qty guard (risk_engine.py:221) stops mattering. 
⛔ TRAP — do NOT unlock fractional by reusing `intent.rebalance`: that flag ALSO exempts the daily-order + open-order throttles (see the comment on OrderIntent). Marking earnings entries as rebalances would silently disable two risk caps as a side effect. 
SCOPE: OrderIntent -> ExecutionService.submit -> RiskEngine.validate -> brokers/base.PlaceOrderRequest -> alpaca.aplace_order body. That's the sacred path => own PR + TWO adversarial reviewers ([[review-agents-opus]] split mandate). Exits are unaffected (they sell a known qty read from the live position — nothing to size).

✅ IN PROGRESS 2026-07-16 (branch feat/fractional-shares-breadth): shipped as FRACTIONAL-QTY, not native notional orders — a deliberate design pivot. Same outcome (100% deployment, expensive names reachable) with far LESS chokepoint surface: no new PlaceOrderRequest.notional field, no adapter notional branch, and — critically — it REUSES the already-proven fractional-qty path (momentum runs on it, so the submit→fill→managed→attribution pipeline already handles fractional). Because we already fetch a live price in _size_candidate, native notional buys nothing here; and a single source of truth (qty, with notional = qty×price) SIDESTEPS the dual-notional smuggling hole entirely, so the founder-greenlit riskengine-notional-reconciliation card is NOT a blocker (stays valid as independent hardening). 
DESIGN: new OrderIntent.allow_fractional — lifts ONLY the whole-share invariant (risk_engine.py:221), NOT the count throttles (that's the trap the board flagged about reusing intent.rebalance; proven by test_allow_fractional_does_not_exempt_count_throttles). Scoped to percent-of-equity strategies (strategy_scan sets it when notional_pct>0 — today only earnings_drift); static-dollar + phone-proposal + agent-scan paths keep the whole-share floor. 
★ LOAD-BEARING CATCH (found before writing): the EXIT engine floored live_qty (int(math.floor)), so a fractional entry would sell 1 of 1.538 and ORPHAN 0.538 forever (next cycle floors dust→0→qty_below_1→never closes = holds through the print). Fixed: full exits now sell the ENTIRE live qty with allow_fractional; scale-outs + whole-share exits unchanged. 
Files: trading/models.py, order_proposal.py (args→intent plumbing), risk_engine.py (gate), proposal_intake.py (Decimal sizing, 9-dp quantize DOWN, $1 min-notional, fixed int() casts), exit_engine.py (fractional full-exit), signals/strategy_scan.py. 6 new tests + full chokepoint suite green (188 passed), ruff clean. 
RESIDUAL for reviewers: a non-fractionable Alpaca symbol would reject at submit (fail-closed, logged, no position) — near-universal for large caps. Pending TWO adversarial reviewers (chokepoint), then PR.

✅ DUAL ADVERSARIAL REVIEW DONE 2026-07-16 (2 Opus, split mandates). DYNAMIC PROVER: SHIP — 25 attack tests + a 3M-case float round-trip probe + a no-mocks end-to-end dry_run through the real chokepoint; could not break oversell, throttle non-exemption, cap enforcement, or the propose→approve round-trip (all PROVEN-SAFE). STATIC ADVERSARY: SHIP-WITH-FIXES — one real HIGH + both prover NITs, all fixed in-round: (1) HIGH — whole-share AUTO full-exit wired qty "2.0" not "2" (snapshot qty col is REAL → Decimal(str(2.0))=Decimal("2.0")); a decimal-format qty could route a NON-FRACTIONABLE symbol's protective stop-sell through Alpaca's fractional engine → reject → the stop never fills. Fixed: exit qty canonicalized (9-dp quantize on fractional, integer-format Decimal on whole). Hit the common case (all whole-share positions) on the safety-critical sell path — my test missed it because Decimal("10.0")==Decimal("10"). (2) entry sibling — an exact-integer-divide fractional order wired "2.000000000"; now "2". (3) defense-in-depth — the RiskEngine fractional exemption now asserts EQUITY-ONLY (no fractional option contracts; unreachable today but the chokepoint self-defends). +3 regression tests (whole-share exit wires "10"; fractional option rejected; integral fractional wires "2"). 207 chokepoint tests green, ruff clean. PR next. | DONE 2026-07-16: #89 merged + deployed pre-open; proven live at the 09:33 ET scan — 7/7 earnings_drift entries executed as exact-notional fractional qtys (e.g. GEN 374.122109988, PWR 15.641696450), all filled in acct_alpaca_strat1; whole-share wire canonicalization + fractional full-exit shipped in the same round.

cards.title: earnings_drift: does holding ONE EXTRA DAY on AMC reporters pay? (PC experiment briefed)
cards.notes:
2026-07-16. Brief: References/EARNINGS_DRIFT_EXTRA_DAY_EXPERIMENT.md (self-contained, sent to PC). 
QUESTION: exit_lead_td=1 exists ONLY because we couldn't tell BMO from AMC — selling day-of would sometimes land after the print. If a company reports AMC, the print lands hours AFTER that day's close, so we could hold through day D and sell at D's close = ONE EXTRA DAY of drift on a 9-day hold (~+11% more exposure). Never tested. 
★ LIVE FEASIBILITY ALREADY CONFIRMED (this is why it's worth PC time): Finnhub/AV supply the FORWARD session in earnings_calendar.hour — measured live, of 957 future rows **544 (57%) have a known session and 247 (26%) are amc**. And it's AUTHORITATIVE not inferred: companies pre-announce their session weeks ahead ('reporting after market close on July 30'); Finnhub's forward hour IS that schedule. Live design: extra day ONLY where forward hour == amc; fail closed on bmo + the 43% null. No new source, no FMP key, no Yahoo scrape (Yahoo 429s this IP outright — a scraped source that blocks us blocks every future user). 
⚠️ ORCHESTRATOR ERROR WORTH REMEMBERING: I first declared this infeasible because EDGAR can't know the forward session — TRUE but irrelevant; I was checking the wrong source while holding the right one. Worse, I read the 92% EDGAR-vs-Finnhub agreement as 'EDGAR is 92% reliable' when Finnhub was the REFERENCE — all 5 disagreements were EDGAR's filing lag, i.e. **Finnhub was right 5/5**. 
⚠️ THE TRAP for the BACKTEST: it must derive the historical session from EDGAR acceptanceDateTime (Finnhub has no history — rolling 30d window), and that is DIRECTIONALLY BIASED: you cannot file an 8-K before you release, so the stamp is a LOWER BOUND on lateness — ~7% of EDGAR's 'amc' calls (2 of 28) are really BMO filed late. Those get held THROUGH their print in the sim => their extra-day return contains a real earnings gap. CONSERVATIVE direction => the measured value is a FLOOR (live uses Finnhub's clean forward hour). Say it, don't silently correct it. 
DESIGN: (1) add `accepted_at TEXT` to research/earnings.py's schema — store the RAW stamp NOT a derived label (re-derivable under stricter rules without a refetch); reuse signals/earnings_edgar.py::session_hour so live/research can't drift (⚠️ UTC->ET conversion FIRST). (2) arm: exit_idx = jn when amc else jn - exit_lead_td; ⚠️ ONLY when bars[jn]['d'] == next_e exactly (holiday => jn is the day AFTER the report). (3) 4 pre-registered arms incl. **Arm D = extra day on EVERYTHING (deliberately wrong) as the NEGATIVE CONTROL** — if D isn't visibly worse than A, the labelling or exit indexing is broken. (4) THE DIAGNOSTIC: extra-day return close[jn]/close[jn-1]-1 split by label — a true AMC extra day is tight pre-report drift; a false one contains the earnings gap (fat/bimodal). The bmo bucket's same-window return IS a post-report return by construction = a free reference for what a gap day looks like. If amc resembles bmo, the labels are junk. 
Costs unchanged (the arm moves the exit, it does NOT add a trade — do not add a round trip).

✅ RESULT 2026-07-15 (PC, post-main-merge): **THE EXTRA DAY PAYS. SHIP IT.** +0.227%/trade conditional on AMC (block CI [+0.058,+0.402], p=0.005) = a ~25% EV lift on ~half the book; **+0.110%/trade portfolio-wide** ([+0.025,+0.198], p=0.007) ≈ +12% overall. And it's a FLOOR — live uses Finnhub's clean forward hour. Branch: origin/research/decision-engine-data-layer (5719359); runner research/_edgehunt/extra_day_experiment.py. 
★ EQUIVALENCE CHECK PASSED — arm A reproduced the stored validated dataset EXACTLY (n=6,624, mean +0.8900%), so the deltas sit on the real baseline, not a re-derivation. Data: full EDGAR refetch, 53,315 events, 100% stamped; labels 3,235 amc / 3,054 bmo / 335 dmh, zero unknown; the holiday bar-alignment guard bit twice (6,622/6,624). session_hour IMPORTED from PR #86 so backtest and live can't drift. 
★ THE DIAGNOSTIC WORKED — amc extra-day stdev **3.19** (tails -8.65/+9.63) vs the bmo gap-day reference **7.15** (-21.04/+18.19). The amc bucket looks NOTHING like a post-report day => labels clean. And **arm C (contamination-cleaned, 16:00-17:30 filings) matches arm B** (+0.101 vs +0.110) => the ~7% late-filed-BMOs do NOT drive the result. 
★ NEGATIVE CONTROL BEHAVED — arm D (extra day on EVERYTHING) has a HIGHER mean (+1.065; post-blowout names carry positive surprises) but significance DIES (CI spans zero, p=0.25), win rate drops 57.8%->56.3%, variance explodes = a lottery ticket, correctly identified. Confirms the sim genuinely sees announcement risk. 
★★ UNEXPECTED + OPERATIONALLY IMPORTANT: **most of the value arrives in the OVERNIGHT GAP into day D** — the day-D-OPEN exit is MORE significant than the close (Δ+0.098 [+0.065,+0.169], p<0.0001 vs p=0.007). ⇒ **the exact intraday exit timing on day D is NOT load-bearing** — we do NOT need market-on-close precision from a loop-driven exit engine. De-risks the implementation. 
⚠️ FOLLOW-UP (does NOT affect this delta — both arms share the same 6,624 setups): the run quantified a long-known gap for the first time — **only 654/909 symbols resolve to a CIK**, so ~28% of the universe (delisted names) has Norgate bars but NO earnings dates => absent from the dataset entirely. **'Survivorship-free' is true of the BARS and NOT of the EARNINGS COVERAGE**; the validated +0.89%/trade is conditioned on 'still listed today'. Direction unknown (acquisitions drift up, bankruptcies down; S&P names are acquired far more often than they fail) and never measured. research/earnings.py:224 has always flagged it ('current EDGAR ticker map — delisted names are expected gaps'; _print_coverage prints 'survivor-gap — do not silently drop in filters'). Fix = predecessor-CIK resolution — the same mechanism as the XOM->CIK 34088 case in [[edgar-free-earnings-source]]. 
⚠️ ALSO: _resolve_cik strips Norgate's delisted suffix (XLNX-202202 -> XLNX) and looks it up in the CURRENT map. Today that fails closed. But if a delisted ticker is ever REUSED by a different company it would silently return the WRONG company's earnings dates — fails OPEN. 
NEXT: implement the live gate — extra day ONLY where the forward hour == 'amc', fail closed on bmo/dmh/null (43% of forward rows have no hour). That's exit_lead_td=0 for amc, 1 otherwise.

✅ SHIPPED 2026-07-16 (PR #86) — the AMC extra-day gate + TWO PRE-EXISTING EXIT BUGS the work exposed. All in signals/exit_evaluators.py — **no chokepoint change**. 
★ MECHANISM (founder's idea, verified): no OPG/TIF field needed. execution_service.py:199 already hardcodes time_in_force='day', and Alpaca's docs say *'Orders not eligible for extended hours submitted after 4:00pm ET will be queued up for release the next trading day'* => submit after the close on jn-1 and the broker fills it at report-day's OPEN. (OPG would have needed a new OrderIntent field AND is REJECTED if submitted 09:28-19:00 ET — the founder's day-order route is simpler and has a wider window.) Everything else was already in place: the exit engine runs inside the 24/7 _poll_loop (api/main.py:529, no market-hours gate); the same loop refreshes the snapshot every 20s so RiskEngine's _SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE=5min gate passes overnight; trading/market_hours.py already exports is_market_open/is_after_close; and exit_engine._exit_in_flight (:109) already blocks a duplicate sell while the order sits queued. 
⚠️ BUG 1 (PRE-EXISTING, FIXED): now_iso() is **UTC**, and today[:10] took the UTC date — which rolls at 20:00 ET. For a Thu print the exit fired **20:01 ET TUESDAY**, queued, and filled at WED's OPEN while the backtest exits at WED's CLOSE. **Live silently forfeited a full session of drift on every trade — live was never the validated strategy.** Fixed: all dates are now the ET calendar date. ⚠️ Subtlety my brief MISSED and the implementer caught: _trading_days_until does its own from_date[:10], so td had to be fed today_key too — fixing only the filter would have left bug 1 alive inside the td computation and looked correct.

⚠️ A PASSING TEST ENCODED BUG 1: tests/test_exit_engine.py:249 pinned today='2026-06-22T12:00Z' (Mon 08:00 ET, PRE-OPEN) and asserted EXIT. The implementer moved the stamp rather than weaken the rule — a green test asserting buggy behaviour is exactly what pressures the next person into 'fixing' the rule instead. 
RULES (all fail closed — anything not exactly 'amc' takes the non-amc path): td==0 -> EXIT unconditionally (backstop); td==1 + amc -> exit only after the close (queues -> report-day OPEN, capturing the overnight gap = +0.206 of the +0.227); td==1 + bmo/dmh/unknown -> exit only when the market is OPEN and >= 15:45 ET (fills near the close as the backtest models) and **must NOT fire after the close** (a queued day order releases at report-day's open = AFTER a bmo print). 
★ NICE PROPERTY: if the engine misses the AMC after-close window, the report_day backstop fires pre-open on report day and the day-TIF order still fills at that day's OPEN — the same target. The backstop costs AMC nothing; only bmo pays. 
⚠️ OPERATIONAL: the bmo exit window is **15:45-16:00 ET (15 min, ~45 loop passes)**. A deploy/restart straddling it means that name rides to the report_day backstop and eats its print. **Don't deploy in the last 15 minutes of a session.** Widening the window costs ~0.015%/trade (drift ~0.1%/day) if that trade-off is ever wanted.

⚠️⚠️ THE LEVELS ARE FICTION, ONLY RANKINGS ARE VALID: linear accrual marks open trades as a straight ramp => suppresses daily vol => INFLATES Sharpe and SHALLOWS every trough (real maxDD WILL exceed these); plus the builder fills at signal close while live fires intraday. A Sharpe of 3.07 (ex-2020) is NOT REAL — no equity strategy sustains that; 1.47 is fiction too. NEVER surface these to the user as calibrated ([[decision-engine-honesty-redteam]]). 
✅ DECISION: fixed fraction, 50 slots, **5%** (~13.5% CAGR / ~13.2% model DD) NOT 10% (20.4%/21.1%). Three optimisms compound the same way (linear accrual understates DD, close fills are optimistic, zero live trades). The fraction can be raised any day after a measured season; a 30% live drawdown can't be un-lived. What kills this product is the founder losing trust, not a bad quarter. ARM WITH: notional_pct=5, max_concurrent_positions=50, max_deployed_usd=100000 (= equity; higher = unmodelled leverage).

⚠️ ROUND 4 2026-07-16 — THE 5% RECOMMENDATION WAS WRONG. Founder challenged both agents; he won. REVISED: **10 slots x 10%** (notional_pct=10, max_concurrent=10, max_deployed=100000). 
What was wrong: (a) the orchestrator's '~37% DD at 95% deployed' was FABRICATED — extrapolated linearly, never measured; the scenario CANNOT HAPPEN (deployment is signal-limited, tops out ~20% CAGR / ~22% DD). (b) 'scales proportionally, Sharpe untouched' FALSE: measured 35%->53% deployment scaled CAGR 1.46x but DD 1.66x and Sharpe FELL — because **drawdowns happen when the book is FULL** (earnings clusters coincide with market stress). Sizing is about WORST-MOMENT deployment, not average. (c) The reflex: models pattern-match to 'recommend the lower-drawdown option' because it sounds responsible. ⚠️ For capital the founder won't touch with no withdrawals, **maxDD is a PSYCHOLOGICAL statistic, not an economic one** — 50x5% is a comfort purchase costing ~7% CAGR/yr compounding (~$758k vs ~$1.86M over the window). 10% is the GROWTH-OPTIMAL point (CAGR peaks there); above it you lose return AND add DD. 20.4%/21.1% DOMINATES SPY on both axes (~20% vs 13% CAGR, ~21% vs 34% DD). 
★ THE ONE SURVIVING ARGUMENT IS DETECTION, NOT COMFORT: the deeper your NORMAL drawdown, the harder it is to detect a DEAD EDGE (at 5% a 20% DD screams; at 10% it's a Tuesday, so you'd sit through it and find out much deeper in). cards.title: Flow engine ran on 0.7% of the chain — bare snapshot = 100 alphabetical contracts, SPY/QQQ/TSLA never saw a put
cards.notes:
THE root data bug, found in the 2026-07-14 data-layer limits audit (founder: 'this is the data, without good data this app is nothing'). poll.py called adapter.get_option_chain_snapshot(u) BARE; the method defaults to limit=None/max_pages=1 = Alpaca's own page default of 100 contracts ALPHABETICAL. An OCC sorts expiry -> C before P -> strike, so one bare page = the nearest expiry, CALLS ONLY. MEASURED live 2026-07-14: SPY has 13,730 contracts / 35 expiries / 6,865 puts and we saw 100 calls at one expiry = 0.7% of the chain. 11 of 30 underlyings NEVER saw a put (AMD,CRWD,GLD,GS,KLAC,MU,NBIS,QQQ,SPCX,SPY,TSLA — it hits the MOST liquid names hardest, since more strikes means the page fills with calls before reaching P); 22 of 30 saw one expiry. IMPACT: aggregate_directional_pressure tracks call_net/put_net, so put_net was STRUCTURALLY ZERO for our three biggest names — every SPY/QQQ/TSLA directional read was bullish by construction. A signal fabricated by omission. ACTIVE_SET_PER_UNDERLYING=60 never once selected on merit; it picked 60 from a pre-truncated alphabetical 100, which is why every cap we debated was downstream of a gutted pool. ⚠️ WE ALREADY KNEW: BUILD.md 2026-07-09 records the identical diagnosis ('unfiltered snapshot pages alphabetically -> one expiry, no puts') — found and fixed in the CHAIN VIEWER only (options_chain.py: expiration_date + limit=1000 + max_pages=3, live-verified NVDA 25 expirations x 86 strikes both sides). The poll was never carried across, and the method docstring enshrined it: 'Defaults (no filter, one page) keep the original single-page behavior the poll's active-set relies on.' The UI the founder reads manually was correct; the engine meant to think for him was not. FIX: page the chain (CHAIN_SNAPSHOT_PAGE_LIMIT=1000 vendor max, CHAIN_SNAPSHOT_MAX_PAGES=20; SPY needs 14 = 1.16s, whole watchlist ~16s per 300s refresh, ~0.3% of the 10,000/min REST budget) + the pager now WARNS when it truncates instead of dropping the tail silently. VERIFIED against the LIVE chain: active set = 1000 contracts, 395 puts / 605 calls, 30 underlyings, 29 distinct expiries; SPY now 20 puts / 16 calls (was 0 puts). 196 tests green, ruff clean. New test is a true behavioural repro (old code fails: 'one page IS the vendor's alphabetical default — no puts'). CONSEQUENCE FLAGGED: ~1,800 contracts now rank active vs the 1,000 sub budget, so STREAM_TRADES_MAX binds HARD for the first time (~33-36 per underlying). Vendor acked 1,506 and the client has ~150x headroom, so 1000->1500 is probably free — unverified; a 405 would now surface via PR #72's error-frame logging. See References/DATA_LAYER_LIMITS_AUDIT_2026-07-14.md. Land AFTER the close (multiplies the candidate pool ~50x; not a market-hours change). cards.title: Flow watcher was blind through the open (trade_subs=0 at the bell) — OI seed + open-aware resubscribe
cards.notes:
Found while reading the 2026-07-14 open probe. Prod's OPRA stream carried ZERO trade subscriptions through the bell — confirmed with no probe interference on 7/10: msgs=0 / trade_subs=0 at 13:30:21, 13:31:22, 13:32:22, first data only 13:33:22. We were missing the first ~2-3 min of every session, the most informative flow window, BY ACCIDENT. Two stacked causes: (a) signals/options_flow/poll.py _refresh_active_set ranks contracts by latestTrade 'today', which at the bell is empty BY CONSTRUCTION (state.oi was never wired to seed membership, only to enrich); (b) signals/options_flow/stream.py SUB_REFRESH_SECONDS=300 is anchored to CONNECT time, not the market clock — the only forced refresh is at connect (~15 min pre-open, session='pre' => empty set), so the first post-open re-check landed 0-5 min late, drifting daily. FIX (this PR): seed the active set from prior-session OI when the today-trade ranking is empty (_refresh_oi already runs first on the opening tick, so no market-hours gate change needed), and force a resubscribe the moment the set turns non-empty instead of waiting out the 5-min grid. Seed is sized to STREAM_TRADES_MAX/underlyings — the whole watchlist seeds at once (25x60=1,500 > the 1,000 budget) and _desired_trades() clips ALPHABETICALLY, which would have silently dropped whole underlyings from the back of the alphabet. 4 new tests: 2 are true old-bug repros verified to fail on the old code with the exact production symptom (active set is literally set() at the bell; 'stream stayed unsubscribed after the active set filled'). The other 2 are guards, not repros — the budget-cap test pins a failure mode THIS change introduces (against old code it errors on the monkeypatch, not behaviourally, since there is no seed to overflow), and the prefers-today-trades test passes on old code by construction (guards the new seed from shadowing live prints). ruff + 174 options_flow tests green. VERIFY AT THE NEXT OPEN: trade_subs>0 in the 13:30 stats line, and prod's own lag_p50/p95 across 13:30-13:32 settles branch W vs C for free (see flow-wildcard-probe). NOT covered: being live at 13:30:00.000 still needs a pre-open warmup path (the poll job's market-hours gate + a ~30s tick + a 25-underlying REST chain walk); deferred — the window it recovers is the one where Alpaca's feed is 3-6s stale anyway. DEPLOYED 2026-07-14 16:20 UTC (PR #71, 884fa29). Card stays in_progress: merged+deployed != verified — the bell verify (trade_subs>0 in the 13:30 stats line, plus lag_p50/p95 across 13:30-13:32 settling branch W vs C) happens at the 2026-07-15 open.

cards.title: Flow stream: reconcile subscriptions against server acks (silent-blindness alarm)
cards.notes:
Follow-up hardening from the PR #71 review (flow-open-blindness): the deepest lesson of the open-blindness bug is that the stream sat silently unsubscribed for weeks because it ignores Alpaca's 'subscription' echo and post-handshake 'error' frames — _subscribed_trades is optimistic (assumes every subscribe succeeded). cards.notes:
